root.name: Italian Game: Paris Defense
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 d6

overview: Black defends e5 with ...d6, a Philidor-like set-up that is solid but passive and hems in the c8 bishop. White usually takes the centre with 4.d4 exd4 5.Nxd4 or plays c3 and d4 with a space edge. Black aims for ...Nf6, ...Be7 and castling, waiting to equalise with ...Bd7 and ...O-O or a later ...d5.

white_ideas.idea: Take the centre with d4 and gain space
Develop with c3, Nbd2 or O-O, then d4 when ready
Avoid early simplification and keep pressure on f7

black_ideas.idea: Hold e5 solidly and develop with ...Nf6 and ...Be7

typical_structures.structure: Philidor-style: Black pawns d6 and e5 against White centre pawns on e4 and d4

character.notes: Passive and hard to attack, but gives White a space edge; few tactics for either side.

soundness.notes: Sound but slightly passive; White is a bit more comfortable.

structure.notes: Tension in the centre that may open after d4; not locked.

approach.notes: Standard but uncommon; a respectable solid choice.

level.notes: Straightforward development; some understanding of Philidor structures.

sublines_that_differ.name: 4.d4
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 d6 4. d4 exd4 5. Nxd4
sublines_that_differ.how: Open centre with a lead for White in space.

character.reason: Black's compact set-up is hard to break down.

structure.reason: Centre stays in tension and often opens after d4.

approach.reason: Less common but a respectable line.

level.reason: Simple moves but Philidor-like plans need understanding.

plans.reason: White gains space in the centre while Black stays compact.
